title: St. Gall Incantations (Cod. Sang. 1395 p. 419): the cryptic colophon

documents.shelfmark: St. Gallen, Stiftsbibliothek, Cod. Sang. 1395, p. 419 (blank verso of the Matthew leaf, e-codices csg-1395)
documents.date: unknown (early medieval; the codex gathers fragments dated 5th-10th century)

plaintext.source: Stokes and Strachan, Thesaurus Palaeohibernicus II (1903), p. 290: the line is read praedicent omnibus nationibus (cf. Matth. 28:19). Read here from the Wikisource scan and maryjones.us, not from the printed volume.

transcription.source: Thesaurus Palaeohibernicus II p. 290 as on Wikisource and maryjones.us; letter count and word breaks checked against the e-codices image of p. 419 (not re-transcribed glyph by glyph)
transcription.notes: The line is in capital-like letters with Greek and odd forms (round e, phi, a pi-like glyph, lunate sigma). The printed transcription renders some glyphs with Greek letters; the image was read only for word breaks and the ending KHAATYONIBVS : FINIT.

system.summary: A one-line cryptic colophon among the St. Gall Incantations: Latin written largely with substituted letter forms. In the printed reading, only the vowels (o, i, u) and s of omnibus differ from plain letters; the mapping for the rest was not worked out here.
system.notes: Printed forms prechnytosan / omnibus / nationibus: the two longer words show 12 glyphs for 10 letters, one for omnibus 7 for 7. No letter table was recovered here; the cipher type is open.

prior_solution.where: Stokes and Strachan, Thesaurus Palaeohibernicus II (1903), p. 290

conditions.human_role: Set the goal 'solve The St. Gall Cryptograms' without naming a text, then described them as computus-manuscript strings (not found), and later asked for the write-up, commit and push.
tools: built-in browser for e-codices IIIF crops

solution.what: Searched the repository, catalogue, leads and the web for a target called the St. Gall Cryptograms: none exists; the nearest St. Gallen cryptogram is the colophon of the St. Gall Incantations (Cod. Sang. 1395), already read by Stokes and Strachan.

Checked the user's description (short strings of non-standard letters in computus manuscripts) and one search-engine claim of a cipher on p. 58 of Cod. Sang. 459; neither exists (p. 58 is an Easter-table page).
Located the colophon on e-codices csg-1395 p. 419 (IIIF) and cropped the line at full resolution.

Compared the printed transcription with the image (word breaks, ending KHAATYONIBVS : FINIT) and tested the published reading letter by letter: omnibus is matched (o, i, u, s written as odd forms); nationibus fits with an extra leading K and a doubled A; praedicent does not align.
Tried to derive the letter table from the 31-glyph line by word-length and glyph comparison; too short to test a key, none recovered.

outcome.method_basis: Stokes and Strachan (1903) printed the reading praedicent omnibus nationibus; here the printed transcription was matched to the e-codices image for word breaks and endings, and the reading was taken from the print without a recovered letter table.
outcome.fraction_read_source: The whole colophon (three words and FINIT) is read in the printed edition; none of it was independently deciphered here.
outcome.notes: Nothing is added to the published reading. The letter-level key is not recovered here: the first word does not align letter for letter with praedicent, and the leading K and doubled A of the last word are unexplained. Whether this line is what the user meant by the St. Gall Cryptograms is unknown.

credits.note: Read the cryptic line as praedicent omnibus nationibus (Thesaurus Palaeohibernicus II, p. 290), known here through Wikisource and maryjones.us, not from the printed volume
credits.source: Whitley Stokes and John Strachan, Thesaurus Palaeohibernicus II (1903), p. 290

texts.label: Cryptic colophon among the St. Gall Incantations
texts.summary: A closing line in cryptic letters among the Irish incantations, read in print as a Gospel commission: let them preach to all nations.
